_comment: The GPU half of the pair. colab_az_cpu.json is this file shrunk to two vCPUs - same encoder, same network, same Gumbel search - so a run can move between them and keep one lineage. train.py picks this file when it finds a GPU and the CPU one when it does not. colab_az_15gb.json is the older PUCT config and does NOT continue this run.
_iterations: The run resumed at iteration 400 with 9736 optimiser steps already spent. 440 more iterations at 160 steps each lands on the 80000-step horizon, so the cosine finishes instead of being cut off a quarter of the way down.
_total_steps: Must be stated, not derived. The fallback is iterations * steps, which after raising iterations would stretch the horizon to 134400 and hold the learning rate high for a run that has already decayed.
_full_frac: Higher than the PUCT config on purpose: playout cap randomisation pays off when the full search is many times costlier than the cheap one, and Gumbel narrows that gap from 192-vs-40 to 24-vs-8. Recording more moves is now the cheaper way to buy samples.
_save_every: latest.pt is ~230 MB and Drive is a FUSE mount, so writing it every iteration spends real minutes on I/O. Every 5 caps the work a disconnect can undo at five iterations.
_gate_every: Was every 5, so a 500-iteration run gated 100 times; at the false-promotion rate below that turned best.pt into a random walk. Every 20 keeps ~22 gates over this run.
_gate_threshold: 48 games at 0.55 needs 27/48, which an evenly-matched candidate reaches 26% of the time - and two candidates are gated (live and ema) with the better one taken, so ~45% of gates promoted noise. 64 games at 0.60 needs 39/64: 5.2% false per candidate, ~10% for the pair, while still catching a genuinely 65%-strong net 79% of the time.
_baseline: After each promotion, measure the new champion against fixed bots. Unlike arena Elo, these numbers stay comparable across the whole run.
